passages.section: Section 0. What the agent starts with
passages.text: Section 0. What the agent starts with. Every transaction carries a `risk_score` between 0 and 1 from the bank's detection model. The model is useful and imperfect: many high scores are legitimate, and some fraud scores low. A score is a reason to look, never a verdict. The only confirmed outcomes are in the closed cases.

Things to know. - **A risk score is a reason to look.** Never a verdict. - **Half the cases are legitimate.** Many look suspicious. An agent that blocks everything scores badly. - **The known patterns are not the only ones.** Some activity in this data fits none of the five. Noticing it and describing it in your own words is scored. - **Devices and regions connect people.** A device profile or a billing region shared across many cards in a short window is worth a look. Some cases can only be solved by asking what happened on *other* cards. - **The V, C, D, M and numeric id columns are real model features with no names.** You may use them as signals. Say so in your evidence rather than pretending to know what V127 means. - **Customer and analyst replies are not provided.** If your agent asks the customer or requests step-up authentication, simulate the response in your own system and record what you assumed in `evidence_requests`.

assessment.reasoning: Transaction 3611043 ($3,008.76) on card C02502-K2 was triggered by a legacy real-time risk score of 0.79. However, the bank's calibrated second-generation fraud model scores this transaction at 0.001 with a historical fraud rate of only 0.0063 (0.63%), showing that this profile is overwhelmingly legitimate. The transaction took place in-person in region 123, which is the card's dominant historical region (1,431 of 2,405 prior transactions) and exhibits a below-average fraud lift of 0.63. Furthermore, holder C02502-K2|123|183 has zero prior transactions in confirmed fraud cases, and this charge directly matches the holder's baseline established just 67 minutes prior by transaction 3611104 ($3,025.17) in the same channel, region, and product category. Although card C02502-K2 experienced out-of-region card-present fraud in October 2016, those prior cases were confined to unfamiliar regions. Similar model alerts on large dollar purchases (CC-3639, CC-3761, and CC-1878 on this card) were cleared after cardholder verification. The evidence indicates this alert is a false alarm on legitimate cardholder spend.
